sources.citation: WALS Online, language Logoti (wals_code_lgt; ISO log; logo1259). Sources cited: Madragule 1986; Tucker 1967; Tucker & Bryan 1966.
sources.note: No values for stress features 14A-17A; Logoti is not in the Goedemans & van der Hulst stress chapters.

sources.citation: Tucker, A. N. 1934. Survey of the language groups in the Southern Sudan. Bulletin of the School of Oriental Studies 7(4): 861-896 (Logo section pp. 867-868).
sources.note: Logo passage is demographic/classificatory only (Logo-Agambi, Logo-Doka, Bari-Logo, Dongo-Tedemu; Keliko and Logo mutually understandable). The only stress remark (p. 891, 'Dynamic accent.. plays a far bigger part in grammar than syllable pitch.. soon all these languages will be entirely stress-languages and not tone-languages in the Sudanic sense') concerns the Nilo-Hamitic group, not Moru-Madi/Logo.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page logo1259 (Logo) and Glottolog hh.bib entries for Logo [log] (local copy.
sources.note: Bibliography only. Adds to the 13 Glottolog refs: Agasuru/Kaloma 1981 (comparative phonology Logoti-Lugbarati, ISP Bukavu); Vallaeys 1986 Dictionnaire logo-français (MRAC); Costermans 1955 Logo-Avokaya als taalgroep; Bokula & Irumu 1994 bibliography/wordlists; Boone & Watson 1999. hh.bib shows Irumu 1986, Madragule 1986, Goyvaerts 1983 and Wright 1995 exist as PDFs in the private Glottolog/MPI collection ('bestfn' fields), not online.

sources.citation: Boone, Douglas W. & Richard L. Watson (eds.). 1999 [1996]. Moru-Ma'di survey report. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 1999-001. Nairobi: SIL Sudan Branch (21-page condensed report).
sources.note: No occurrence of 'stress' or 'accent' anywhere in the text. Tone is mentioned as marked in the Logo/Lugbara wordlists; the Ogambi dialect of Logo 'differs from its four closest co-dialects mainly in tones, primarily word final tones'. Silent on stress.

sources.note: Checked in case it was the 1983 MSU volume containing Goyvaerts; it is not. Logo appears only in two comparative wordlist lines ('Ma'di, Logo -zi'). Nothing on stress.

tone.says: 396-page Logo-French dictionary with French-Logo index and 24 pages of front matter (MRAC Archives d'anthropologie 29, 1986), the companion lexicon to Vallaeys' 1988 Grammaire logo (a work listed here); whether headwords carry tone marks and whether the introduction states a tone inventory is unverified (no open copy; Glottolog holds only an internal PDF; Kutsch Lojenga's 1989 JALL 11(1) review, a work listed here, inside the De Gruyter REVIEWS block DOI 10.1515/jall.1989.11.1.89, would settle…
